name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate

card.summary: Acetylated, amidated Semax analog sold as a research chemical; no direct studies.

quick.overview:
N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a chemically modified version of the peptide Semax. The modifications are meant to make it last longer in the body.

No studies of this exact compound are reported, and it has no studied appearance use.
quick.mechanism: It is presumed to act like Semax, which is described as affecting neurotrophin (BDNF, NGF) expression in animal studies; this has not been tested for the modified form. Intranasal use is the route typically described.
quick.risks: It is sold for laboratory use and is not approved for human use in most jurisdictions. Safety in people has not been studied.

lead: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Semax, sold by research-chemical suppliers as a longer-lasting, intranasally used nootropic. It has no direct effect on the face or body; people who take interest in it do so for focus, mood and mental drive, hoping these support consistent training, skincare and other self-improvement routines [1][2].

Its sequence is Ac-Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, a Semax backbone with an acetyl cap at the N-terminus and an amide at the C-terminus, changes described as intended to resist enzymatic breakdown [1]. Semax itself is a synthetic analogue of the ACTH(4-10) fragment, first described in the scientific literature in 1991, and is a prescription drug in Russia, where it was included on the List of Vital and Essential Drugs on 7 December 2011 [2].

The modified compound is supplied for laboratory use and is not approved for human therapeutic use. Claimed benefits are extrapolated from Semax research; no direct studies of this variant are reported [1]. Semax is not evaluated, approved or marketed in most countries outside Russia and Eastern Europe, and is sold online as a purported nootropic [2].

chain: Intranasal peptide analog taken as a nootropic
Claimed effects on focus, mood and stress via neurotrophin pathways
Better adherence to training and self-care routines
angle.text: There is no direct appearance effect. Users who write about Semax-family peptides on bodybuilding forums describe them as mental-performance aids that they hope support gym and lifestyle consistency.

infobox: Semax, Russian ACTH(4-10) analog; prescription in Russia [2]

paras: Semax is described as having poor oral bioavailability and is given as a nasal spray or by subcutaneous injection; online vendors market it as a nootropic [2]. Reference text describes N-Acetyl Semax Amidate as primarily used intranasally in research settings [1]. On T Nation, forum members have mentioned Semax in nootropic and wellbeing discussions, including a thread asking whether it affects libido [4], a reply suggesting it alongside methylene blue [5], and a 2015 thread titled as an article from way back on Semax [6]. A 2010 nootropics thread also lists many cognitive supplements [3].

The acetyl group at the N-terminus is described as blocking aminopeptidases, and the amide at the C-terminus as blocking carboxypeptidases [1]. The stability benefits are described as hypothesized and unverified for this specific compound [1]. The backbone is the Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro sequence of Semax, itself an ACTH(4-10) analogue with a Pro-Gly-Pro tail [1][2].

The mechanism of unmodified Semax is described as unknown. Animal studies report increased brain-derived neurotrophic factor and its receptor TrkB in the hippocampus, activation of serotonergic and dopaminergic systems, and antidepressant-like and anxiolytic-like effects; it may interact with melanocortin receptors and inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes [2]. Whether the modified analog behaves the same way has not been tested [1].

In Russia Semax is a prescription drug indicated, per Wikipedia, for stroke, transient ischemic attack, memory and cognitive disorders, peptic ulcers, optic nerve disease and immune support [2]. Wikipedia cites a 2006 study as showing cognitive effects but gives no clinical trial results for stroke or cognition [2]. A product listing in the US describes it as not FDA approved and unscheduled [2]. N-Acetyl Semax Amidate has no regulatory approval and is sold under research-use labelling [1].
No studies found on N-Acetyl Semax Amidate itself. Findings on unmodified Semax come mainly from Russian clinical use and animal work [1][2].

timeline.event: Semax first described in the scientific literature [2].
Semax added to the Russian List of Vital and Essential Drugs (7 December) [2].

lore.intro: Semax-family peptides come up in forum nootropic and hormone threads on T Nation, usually as passing mentions [3][4][5].

claims.believers: A 2022 T Nation poster says they read that Semax helped many people with libido and asked whether others had experienced it [4].
claims.experts: No published trials have tested Semax or its acetylated analog for libido [1][2].

claims.claim: Semax is a useful nootropic add-on.
claims.believers: Forum members mention it alongside other cognitive supplements [3].
claims.experts: Semax is prescribed in Russia for stroke and cognitive disorders; animal studies report neurotrophin effects, and the analog has no direct studies [1][2].

claims.claim: Semax can be combined with methylene blue for gut or energy issues.
claims.believers: A 2026 T Nation reply in a testosterone-therapy thread suggests looking up Semax with methylene blue in a list of ideas [5].
claims.experts: No published studies were found on this combination.
